questionText:
The following two signed 2's complement numbers (multiplicand M and multiplier Q) are being multiplied using Booth's algorithm:

M: 1100 1101 1110 1101 and Q: 1010 0100 1010 1010

The total number of addition and subtraction operations to be performed is ________. (Answer in integer)
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

In Booth's Multiplication Algorithm, an addition or subtraction operation is triggered at each step $i$ based on the transition between adjacent bits $(Q_i, Q_{i-1})$ with initial $Q_{-1} = 0$:
• $10_2 \implies$ Subtraction ($-M$)
• $01_2 \implies$ Addition ($+M$)
• $00_2$ or $11_2 \implies$ No operation

Given the 16-bit multiplier $Q = 1010\ 0100\ 1010\ 1010_2$, appending $Q_{-1} = 0$ gives:
$Q_{15}\dots Q_0 Q_{-1} = 1010\ 0100\ 1010\ 1010\ 0_2$

Now, examining all bit pairs $(Q_i, Q_{i-1})$ for $i = 0$ to $15$:
• $i=0: (0,0) \implies$ No Op
• $i=1: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (1)
• $i=2: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (2)
• $i=3: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (3)
• $i=4: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (4)
• $i=5: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (5)
• $i=6: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (6)
• $i=7: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (7)
• $i=8: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (8)
• $i=9: (0,0) \implies$ No Op
• $i=10: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (9)
• $i=11: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (10)
• $i=12: (0,0) \implies$ No Op
• $i=13: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (11)
• $i=14: (0,1) \implies$ Addition (12)
• $i=15: (1,0) \implies$ Subtraction (13)

Counting all transitions ($01$ and $10$), there are 7 subtractions and 6 additions.

Thus, the total number of addition and subtraction operations performed is 13.
